questions.q: What does the SFT stage actually train on, and what loss does it use?
options: Preference pairs (chosen/rejected), using the Bradley-Terry loss
A dataset of (prompt, ideal response) demonstration pairs, using ordinary cross-entropy loss on the response tokens
Reward model scores, using a policy-gradient loss
Randomly generated text, using a contrastive loss
questions.explain: SFT is plain supervised fine-tuning on human-written demonstrations — no reward signal or RL is involved at this stage.

questions.q: Why is the reward model in this pipeline initialized from the SFT checkpoint rather than from the raw pretrained base model?
options: It isn't — the reward model is always trained completely from scratch
Because the reward model is trained on preference pairs sampled from the SFT model's own outputs, so building it on the same base weights keeps it aligned with that distribution
Because the pretrained base model has no weights to initialize from
Because TRL's RewardTrainer requires a randomly initialized model
questions.explain: The reward model swaps in a scalar-reward head on top of the SFT weights, keeping it consistent with the model whose outputs it was trained to score.

questions.q: In the PPO stage, what are the two distinct roles the SFT checkpoint is loaded into, and how do they differ?
options: Both are trainable policies updated identically
A trainable policy (with an added value head, updated during training) and a frozen reference model (same weights, never updated, used to measure drift via the KL penalty)
One is the reward model and the other is the demonstration dataset
There is only one role — the SFT checkpoint is used just once
questions.explain: PPO loads the SFT checkpoint both as the trainable policy (plus a value head for advantage estimation) and, separately, as a frozen reference model that never updates.

questions.q: What is the role of AutoModelForCausalLMWithValueHead in this pipeline, and why is it needed?
options: It replaces the reward model entirely
It adds a value-function head on top of the SFT weights, which PPO's advantage estimation (GAE) requires
It is only used during the SFT stage, not during PPO
It removes the language-modeling head so the model can no longer generate text
questions.explain: PPO's advantage estimation needs a value function; this class attaches that value head to the same underlying SFT-derived weights used as the policy.

questions.q: During the PPO stage, is the reward model's own weights ever updated?
options: Yes, the reward model is fine-tuned jointly with the policy at every PPO step
No — the reward model is frozen during PPO and used only to score the policy's generations
Yes, but only every other PPO step
The reward model is discarded entirely once PPO begins
questions.explain: The reward model's weights stay fixed throughout PPO fine-tuning; it is used purely as a scoring function for the policy's generated text.
